findings.title: B1's auth gate has no failure state: a failed anonymous sign-in leaves the receive screen spinning forever instead of the honest retryable verdict
findings.trace: ReceiveScreen.swift:55-58 `.task(id: account.uid ?? "-") { guard account.uid != nil, drop == nil else { return } ; await load() }`. When uid is nil the task returns and NOTHING sets `failure`, so body falls to the else at ReceiveScreen.swift:40-44 and renders an unbounded ProgressView — the only branch with no copy, no Try again, and no Close. uid==nil is an ABSORBING state: AccountService.swift:25-41 `start()` signs in once, and on failure sets statusText at :37 and never retries; AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:28-35 calls `accountService.start()` exactly once from the WindowGroup task, and the scenePhase .active handler at :36-56 refreshes the library (:52) but never re-attempts auth. So a single sign-in failure pins the receive screen for the rest of the process. Round 11's ungated `.task` reached DropSharingService.fetchSharedDrop, whose throw path (DropSharingService.swift:72-74) produced `.unknown` and the retryable screen — the round-12 gate replaced a truthful failure with an unbounded wait.
findings.harm: A first-time recipient — the app's entire acquisition funnel — taps a magic link while on a flaky connection or captive-portal Wi-Fi. Anonymous sign-in fails once; the invitation screen spins indefinitely with no message and no button, even after the network recovers, because auth is never retried in-session. The user's only exit is an undiscoverable swipe-down, and the shared moment is lost. This is exactly the failure the charter forbids: a mechanic that cannot progress presented as progress.
findings.fix: Give the gate a terminal state. Publish an auth phase from AccountService (`enum AuthPhase { case connecting, ready(String), failed }`, set `.failed` in the catch at AccountService.swift:36-39) and add a `retrySignIn()` that re-runs the sign-in. In ReceiveScreen map `.failed` (and a bounded `.connecting` deadline, e.g. 15 s) to `failure = .unknown` so the existing honest copy plus Try again renders; make the Try again action call `account.retrySignIn()` before `load()`. Keep the uid gate for the `.connecting` window only — waiting is correct, waiting forever is not.

findings.title: redeem() treats in-memory presence as proof of on-disk presence, so retrying a link after a failed persist reports success and writes nothing
findings.trace: DropStore.swift:796-805: the in-memory insert at :797 happens BEFORE `try await local.save(drop)` at :799, and the catch at :800-803 sets lastPersistError and rethrows WITHOUT removing the row it just inserted — the inverse of add(), which deliberately persists first and inserts only after success (:822-831, comment at :819-820). The round-12 B4 predicate at :796 then keys the entire write decision on `drops.contains`. Sequence: (1) recipient taps Reveal, RootView.swift:64-72 calls redeem; local.save throws (disk pressure — LocalDropStore.persist at :335-340 or the loadDrops rethrow at :202-203); the user sees 'Couldn't save this drop — it may disappear after this session' (RootView.swift:68-70) and the row stays in `drops`. (2) The user re-opens the same link; redeem runs again; `drops.contains` is now TRUE, the whole persist block is skipped, hadTombstone is false so :813 does nothing, and the function returns normally — no throw, no banner. (3) The next completed cloud read rebuilds `drops` from disk+cloud at :588-591, and the row — on neither — silently disappears mid-session; otherwise it is gone at relaunch. Round 11's predicate keyed on pendingSyncIDs, which the round-12 comment itself notes is structurally empty for received drops (:781-784), so the old code always took the save branch and the retry worked.
findings.harm: A received drop is permanently lost after the user does exactly the right thing. The first attempt tells the truth ('may disappear'); the retry fabricates success; the drop then vanishes with no message at all. Data loss plus a fabricated receipt in one flow — both charter red lines.
findings.fix: Make the authority claim match the fact it asserts. Either (a) mirror add(): persist first, insert into `drops` only after local.save returns, so in-memory presence really does imply on-disk presence; or (b) keep the current order but roll back the insert in the catch at :800-803. (a) is preferable and is the pattern already blessed at :819-820. Additionally track redeem's disk write with the same generation discipline remove() got in round 12 (:872-875) so a superseded redeem cannot report a persist it did not perform.

findings.title: Terminal sync verdicts are never revalidated again: the composed auth-ready pass gates revalidation on a uid change that is structurally impossible on the first pass of a process
findings.trace: DropStore.swift:747-763: `let changed = evidenceUid != nil && evidenceUid != uid` (:748). evidenceUid is per-instance in-memory state (:429) on a DropLibrary created fresh per process (AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:18), so on the ONLY auth-ready call of a launch it is nil and `changed` is false — the revalidation loop at :755-761 never runs. RootView.swift:162-169 calls authDidBecomeReady and nothing else; accountDidChange() (:728-737), which the round-11 sequence ran on every auth-ready firing and which unconditionally re-enqueued every terminal id, is now called from no production site (grep: only DropStoreTests.swift:846). No other path re-attempts a terminal drop: performCloudSync clears it from pendingSyncIDs when it goes terminal (:1022-1023 and :1012-1013), and reconcileCloud only iterates pendingSyncIDs and pendingDeleteIDs (:928-936). The single remaining recovery is manual and per-drop: ShareDropSheet.swift:201-209, reached only by opening that drop's share sheet and tapping Send. terminalSyncFailureIDs is durable (:432, :462-463).
findings.harm: A transient server condition that the taxonomy classifies as non-retryable becomes permanent. Concretely: this app is anonymous-auth-first (AccountService.swift:27-30 reuses the cached user and never re-signs), so an expired/invalidated anonymous token makes Firestore answer UNAUTHENTICATED (gRPC 16), which FirebaseDropStore.swift:249-250 maps to a terminal refusedByServer verdict. Every affected drop is then permanently badged 'can't sync from this account connection' (ProfileScreen.swift:82-91, DropsListScreen.swift:39-46), its magic link stays dead, and no launch, refresh, or background return ever retries — even after auth is healthy again. Round 11 recovered these on the next launch.
findings.fix: Separate the two concerns the round-12 composition merged. Keep the evidence-latch reset gated on `changed`, but run the terminal revalidation on the first auth-ready pass of every session as well: `let firstPassThisSession = evidenceUid == nil` before :749, then `if changed || firstPassThisSession` at :755. This preserves cross-cutting rule 4 — the verdict is still revoked only by a server ack in performCloudSync (:974-976) — while restoring automatic recovery. Consider also surfacing a retry affordance on the DropsListScreen row that already renders the xmark.icloud badge (DropsListScreen.swift:154-159).

findings.title: The round-12 reaction-key drift lock fails open on `let` and attributed stored properties, the exact edits it exists to catch
findings.trace: drift-check.mjs:39-42: the struct body is captured, then fields are extracted with `^\s*var (\w+)\s*[:=]`. Verified empirically against a fixture containing `let sessionTag: String` and `@DocumentID var docRef: String?` — the extractor returned only ['id','emoji','uid','byName','at'], silently omitting both. Swift's synthesized Codable encodes `let` stored properties identically to `var`, so the encoded payload would carry a key the rules' hasOnly list (firestore.rules:78) does not permit. The check then compares equal-length, equal-membership lists and exits 0 (verified: `node drift-check.mjs` → 'reaction key drift check OK'). The emulator suite cannot catch it either: rules.test.mjs:96-98 writes a HARD-CODED reaction payload rather than one derived from appReactionKeys(), so it proves nothing about the shipping struct's shape. Related fragility in the same file: rulesReactionKeys (:44-49) matches the FIRST `keys().hasOnly([...])` anywhere in firestore.rules — the scheduled seams-3 drops field-mask residual would insert one ahead of the reactions block at line 78 and silently retarget the lock.
findings.harm: The lock is the only thing standing between a routine struct edit and total reaction breakage after the v3 deploy. Adding one immutable field to DropReaction (ReactionService.swift:10-16) passes CI, then every reaction write is PERMISSION_DENIED at firestore.rules:78; ReactionService.send throws (:70-73), every viewer's reaction renders 'Couldn't send — it lives in this memory only' (MemoryScreen.swift:183), and the loop's entire payoff dies with a green drift check.
findings.fix: Two changes. (1) Widen and harden the extractor: match `^\s*(?:@\w+(?:\([^)]*\))?\s+)*(?:var|let)\s+(\w+)\s*[:=]` and make the parser fail loudly on any line in the struct body it cannot classify, so it fails closed rather than open. Anchor rulesReactionKeys to the `match /drops/{dropId}/reactions` block instead of the first hasOnly in the file. (2) Better, remove the parser from the critical path: add a Swift unit test that JSON-encodes a DropReaction and asserts its key set equals a pinned literal, and have drift-check read that literal — then the lock is driven by the encoder's actual output rather than by a regex over declaration syntax.

findings.title: cloudProvenIDs is stamped for link-received drops that can never clear it, growing a durable set with no retirement path
findings.trace: DropStore.swift:886-890 marks cloud provenance on `drop.ownerUid != nil || acked || terminal` — but it runs BEFORE the received-drop early return at :896. Every link-received drop carries a stamped ownerUid (DropSharingService.swift:94-96 copies the envelope uid onto the drop), so deleting one always calls markCloudProven (:1165-1169) and persists it to the durable cloudProvenDropIDs key (:435, :1168). No tombstone is created for a received drop (the guard at :896 returns before markPendingDelete at :897), so neither retirement path is reachable: performCloudDelete's ack clear (:1058) and refresh's server-confirmed-absence clear (:693) both require a tombstone to exist.
findings.harm: Durable, monotonically growing UserDefaults state — one UUID string per received-and-deleted drop, forever, on the primary consumption path of the app. No user-visible misbehavior today (the value is only read at :1090 for ids that reached the delete pipeline), but it is a provenance fact recorded about a document this device never owned, which is precisely the kind of stale evidence the round-12 provenance work exists to prevent from outliving its producing condition (cross-cutting rule 4).
findings.fix: Move the markCloudProven block from :886-890 to after the ownership guard at :896, so provenance is recorded only for documents this device is actually about to delete in the cloud. One-line move; the existing test at DropStoreTests.swift:1073-1093 still passes because that drop is owned.

findings.title: Neither emulator suite pins the rules behavior the B2 staged-delete recall depends on: recreating a just-deleted drop via a merge set
findings.trace: The round-11 CRITICAL fix at DropStore.swift:806-816 works only because FirestoreAcked.setData (FirestoreAcked.swift:31-34, merge defaults true) issues a precondition-free patch that the backend evaluates as a CREATE once the serialized staged delete has landed. That is a rules-visible operation — firestore.rules:59-60 for v3, firestore.rules.deployed:34-35 for v2 — and neither suite asserts it. rules.test.mjs covers delete-of-absent (:90-91) and create (:79-80) separately, never the delete-then-recreate-same-id sequence; deployed-rules.test.mjs (5 assertions, :49-64) does not cover it at all. The suites also do not pin the owner-scoped list query the client issues every refresh against the DEPLOYED ruleset (FirebaseDropStore.swift:64-66 vs firestore.rules.deployed:31-33) — that shape is pinned only for v3 (rules.test.mjs:73-74).
findings.harm: If a future rules revision constrains recreation (a common hardening move, e.g. gating create on `resource == null` plus an id-reuse check, or adding a field mask), B2 regresses silently in CI: the user redeems their own deleted drop, the re-upload is refused, and the cloud copy plus every recipient's link stay dead. The client would surface it as a terminal verdict rather than silently, so the blast radius is bounded — but a fix the counsel rated CRITICAL is currently protected by no assertion.
findings.fix: Add one assertion to each suite: in rules.test.mjs, `assertSucceeds` a sequence that deletes drops/new-own as the owner and then re-creates it with `setDoc(..., dropData(OWNER,'link'), { merge: true })`; mirror it in deployed-rules.test.mjs against firestore.rules.deployed so the live ruleset's behavior is pinned too. While there, add the owner-scoped list query shape to the deployed suite so both suites pin the same client dependencies.

testCases.asserts: In both emulator suites, an owner who deletes drops/{id} and then issues setDoc(..., { merge: true }) for the same id with their own ownerUid succeeds.
testCases.failsWhen: Fails whenever a rules revision stops permitting recreation of a deleted document id — the exact condition that silently breaks the B2 staged-delete recall at DropStore.swift:806-816. Today no assertion in either suite covers the sequence, so such a revision ships green; the existing create (rules.test.mjs:79-80) and delete-of-absent (:90-91) assertions both pass with and without the recreation being permitted.

cleanAreas: SharedDropFetch tri-state totality (the lens's primary question): .absent has exactly ONE producer — a served `snapshot.exists == false` at DropSharingService.swift:75 — and every other outcome resolves .unknown: unconfigured Firebase (:66), any thrown error including permission-denied/unauthenticated under the live v2 rules (:72-74), and payload-decode failure (:89-93). `getDocument(source: .server)` cannot produce a snapshot without a server answer, so no client-side condition can fabricate absence. The ReceiveScreen mapping claims no cause on .unknown and offers retry only there (ReceiveScreen.swift:120-141).

Per-row serverConfirmedIDs semantics: `metadata.hasPendingWrites` is a per-document flag that is valid inside query snapshots and is precisely the latency-compensation marker the fix assumes (FirebaseDropStore.swift:81-83). Pairing it with the query-level `!isFromCache` before markAcked (DropStore.swift:557, :563-565) closes the partial-metadata window in both directions — a cache-served query earns nothing regardless of per-row flags, and a server-served query's locally-staged rows earn nothing either. The test double reproduces it faithfully (DropStoreTests.swift:1315).

Delete-refusal taxonomy transfer: audited each terminal code against delete semantics rather than write semantics. Firestore deletes are idempotent — an absent document is an ACK, not notFound — so code 5 on a delete can only originate from a missing database/collection configuration, which is genuinely non-retryable; code 7 is what the live v2 ruleset returns for absent-doc deletes (pinned at deployed-rules.test.mjs:53-54) and correctly resolves to DONE for unproven ids. Codes 4/8/10/13/14 remain retryable and now spend no budget (DropStore.swift:1070-1073). Round 12 is strictly safer here than round 11's spend-on-every-failure.

The FirestoreAcked write seam: `.acked` is earned only by a yielded ack; cancellation, a no-yield stream finish, and the deadline all resolve to `queuedLocally` (FirestoreAcked.swift:85-92, :98, :102-103). An encoder throw is correctly separated as a rejection at :48-53 rather than a queue.

Two-phase publish (DropStore.swift:525-529, :588-592), durable incident memory driven from LoadOutcome (:625-632, :642-653), server-only revocation of lastSyncError (:574), the remove() post-await generation re-check (:872-875), the uncapped listener-prune predicate (ReactionService.swift:119-130), the firstAt FIRST-IN badge including the viewer's own confirmed row (ReactionService.swift:198-206, MemoryScreen.swift:202-204), the SURF-lens-3 Memory copy (MemoryScreen.swift:79-84), the SURF-lens-5 ProfileScreen rung copy (ProfileScreen.swift:103-112 — verified changed, no 'sync is on hold' claim survives), and ShareDropSheet reading liveDrop everywhere (ShareDropSheet.swift:49,52,77,86,116,118,189) all trace clean with tests that fail without the fix.

The non-provenanced CloudRead fallback at DropStore.swift:543-553 would fabricate serverConfirmedIDs for every returned row, but it is unreachable in production: AppConfig.swift:7 pins cloudKitEnabled = false and the Firebase branch wins whenever a config plist exists (DropStore.swift:450-452). Not a finding, but it is the one place where the acked fact is granted without evidence — worth a comment if CloudKit is ever revived.

The emoji drift lock is sound for the current shape and is wired into the gate: package.json:7 runs drift-check before the emulator suites, and it exits non-zero on mismatch (verified by running it; both the emoji and key checks report OK). The deployed v2 reaction rule (firestore.rules.deployed:38-40) imposes no emoji or key constraint, so today's production reactions are unaffected by the drift risk described in seams-4 — that risk arms at the v3 deploy.

closureVerdicts.trace: DropSharingService.swift:65-104 — `.absent` is produced at :75 ONLY from a served `snapshot.exists == false` (the read is forced to `source: .server` at :71); every throw → `.unknown` (:72-74), unconfigured Firebase → `.unknown` (:66), envelope decode failure → `.unknown` (:89-93). ReceiveScreen.swift:120-144 maps `.gone` → "This drop isn't available / taken back or expired" with NO retry, `.unknown` → "This link can't be opened right now… check your connection and try again in a moment" + Try again, claiming no cause. findings.title: remove() abandons its tombstone and cloud delete when ANY concurrent refresh lands during the disk write — the disk row is already gone
findings.trace: remove() bumps and captures the GLOBAL refreshGeneration (:858-859), deletes from disk (:863), then aborts all bookkeeping if the generation moved (:872-875). But refreshGeneration is bumped synchronously at the top of refresh() (:491), and refresh() is fired from four user-reachable places: AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:52 (every scenePhase .active — a round-12 addition), DropsListScreen.swift:26 (the refresh toolbar button, on the SAME screen as the swipe-to-delete at :113-121), MapScreen.swift:105-107 (Explore tab .task), and DropStore.swift:720 (incident Dismiss). Both methods are @MainActor and suspend at their actor hops, so any refresh started while remove() is inside `await local.delete` wins the generation and remove() returns at :875 having: (a) already destroyed the disk row, (b) NOT executed drops.removeAll (:877), (c) NOT cancelled the in-flight upload task (:879-880), (d) NOT captured cloud provenance (:886-890), (e) NOT cleared pending/terminal (:891-892), and critically (f) NEVER reached markPendingDelete/launchCloudDelete (:897-898). The abort is the round-12 STATE-lens-6 change; the branch it added has no test — testDeleteDuringRefreshIsNotResurrectedByThePublish (DropStoreTests.swift:369-389) parks the refresh BEFORE remove bumps, so remove's guard passes and the branch is never entered.
findings.harm: The user's 'take it back' silently never reaches the server. Trigger: swipe-delete a drop on the Sent tab and tap the toolbar refresh (or switch to Explore, or background/foreground the app) while the disk write is in flight. Two outcomes, both charter violations: (1) the uid-scoped cloud read still returns the row, so the deleted drop RESURRECTS in the library with no explanation; (2) if the cloud read does not return it (terminal owner mismatch, cloud read failing), the row vanishes locally and the app reports all-clear while the Firestore document and every shared magic link stay live forever — no tombstone, no unresolved-delete rung, no banner. Aggravation: the un-cancelled in-flight upload task can re-create the cloud document the user just deleted, and the stale pendingSyncIDs entry briefly surfaces as the false 'N changes can't upload' rung (ProfileScreen.swift:114-128).
findings.fix: Do not gate a destructive-intent abort on the global publish generation. Add a per-drop row epoch (`private var rowGenerations: [UUID: UInt64]`) bumped ONLY by add/update/redeem for that id; in remove() capture it before `await local.delete` and re-check only it afterwards. refresh() then cannot abort a delete, while a redeem landing mid-flight still does. If the epoch did move, the correct action is still not a bare return — re-verify whether the row is back on disk and, if it is not, complete the tombstone bookkeeping anyway (the disk row is gone either way).

findings.title: hasCompletedCleanRefresh is never revoked by a destructive local outcome — after Dismiss, the ladder claims 'Synced' over a library quarantined this session
findings.trace: The latch is set at :654-656 when `localProvablyClean && (cloud == nil || cloudReadServerServed)` and is set FALSE in exactly two places: accountDidChange (:731, no production caller) and authDidBecomeReady on a real uid change (:751). `localProvablyClean` (:642-653) correctly returns false for `.skippedRows`/`.quarantinedWholeFile`/`.readFailed`, but a false result only fails to SET the latch — it never clears an already-earned one. Round 12's durable incident memory (:625-632, :649) closes this laundering across launches only, because hasCompletedCleanRefresh is per-instance. Within the session the ProfileScreen ladder is protected solely by the localReadWarning rung (ProfileScreen.swift:103-113), and acknowledgeReadIncident (:706-722) clears that warning while leaving the latch true, so the ladder falls through :145 to the 'Synced — the server has confirmed your drops' rung at ProfileScreen.swift:152-156. Cross-cutting rule 4: the producing condition (provably clean local truth) has demonstrably disappeared and the verdict survives it.
findings.harm: A user whose drops.json becomes whole-file unreadable mid-session sees the corruption banner, taps Dismiss, and is then told 'Synced — the server has confirmed your drops' for the rest of the session over an emptied library. Honest reachability note: this requires in-session corruption (the app itself writes atomically), so the trigger is external — filesystem/IO damage or a restore — not an everyday path; the equivalent cross-launch laundering IS already closed by own-B. The defect is that the same false all-clear the own-B memory was built to forbid remains reachable in the session where the loss actually happened.
findings.fix: Revoke on positive evidence of loss, symmetrically with the memory write at :625-632: in the same switch, `case .skippedRows?, .quarantinedWholeFile?, .readFailed?: hasCompletedCleanRefresh = false` (and set it false on the throwing-load abort at :500-509 as well). This cannot flap — those three outcomes are positive proof local truth is not clean, unlike `.absentFile`, which must keep its current treatment.

findings.title: redeem() throws on a local-save failure before the own-A re-upload enqueue, skipping the staged-delete recall exactly when the local copy is also lost
findings.trace: redeem() clears the tombstone first (:793-795), then for a missing local row inserts and saves (:796-805). If `local.save` throws, :801-802 sets lastPersistError and rethrows — control never reaches the B2 re-upload enqueue at :813-816. The tombstone is already gone, so nothing in the library will ever re-issue or compensate for the delete that is still sitting in Firestore's durable mutation queue. RootView.swift:64-72 catches the throw and shows 'Couldn't save this drop — it may disappear after this session', which describes the local row only.
findings.harm: User deletes their own drop while the ack is unanswered (delete staged), re-opens their own magic link to take it back, and the disk write fails (disk full / protected data). The staged delete then flushes and destroys the Firestore document and every recipient's link, while the app has told the user only that the local copy may not persist. Compound and rare, but the failure is invisible in the one dimension that matters (the shared link) and the fix is mechanical.
findings.fix: Move the own-drop re-upload ahead of the throw, or wrap it in a `defer`: capture `let shouldRecall = hadTombstone && drop.receivedViaLink != true` up front and enqueue the sync (from the fetched copy when no local row survives) before rethrowing the persist error. Recalling the cloud delete does not depend on the local write succeeding.

findings.title: 'Dismiss' now irreversibly DELETES the unreadable rows — no consent, and the sidecar it claims to rely on is never checked
findings.trace: Round 12 turned the banner's acknowledgement into a destructive write. DropStore.swift:263-278 acknowledgeIncident(): for a .skippedRows outcome it re-reads the file (:265), decodes (:266), and calls persist(survivors) (:269) — the unreadable rows are overwritten out of drops.json. The ONLY control on the UI side is DropsListScreen.swift:58-68, a Label carrying library.localReadWarning plus a button literally titled 'Dismiss' (:66) → DropLibrary.acknowledgeReadIncident() (DropStore.swift:706-722) → local.acknowledgeIncident(). Nothing in the label, the button, or any alert tells the user that tapping it destroys rows. The code's own justification — 'their original bytes are already preserved in the digest sidecar' (:260-261) — is an UNCHECKED precondition: preserveUnreadable() (:285-298) returns false when the sidecar write fails (:294-297) and the caller only downgrades the user-facing string (:213-215, dropping '(original kept on disk)'); lastOutcome is still .skippedRows (:218), so acknowledgeIncident's `if case .skippedRows?` at :264 matches and rewrites anyway. The failure mode that produces unreadable rows (a full or failing disk) is the same one that makes the sidecar write fail, so the two are correlated, not independent. Even on the success path the preservation is a dead end: the sidecar lives beside drops.json in Application Support, nothing in the app ever reads a `.unreadable-*` file (grep: preserveUnreadable is the only reference), and Config/Info.plist declares neither UIFileSharingEnabled nor LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace — the user can never reach those bytes. Before round 12 acknowledgement only removed the journal note (:304-306), so the rows survived on disk and a later app version could still have recovered them.
findings.harm: Permanent, unannounced destruction of user data. Trigger: the device is low on free space; drops.json is written with two truncated rows. Launch → banner 'Your saved drops couldn't be read' (no 'original kept on disk' clause, because the sidecar write also failed for lack of space). The user taps a button labelled 'Dismiss' expecting the banner to go away; DropStore.swift:269 rewrites drops.json with the survivors only. Those two drops — their coordinates, captions, recipients and AR placements — are gone from the device with no copy anywhere, and no screen ever said they would be deleted.
findings.fix: (a) Gate the destructive rewrite on verified preservation: record the sidecar URL (or a bool) alongside lastOutcome when preserveUnreadable succeeds, and in acknowledgeIncident require FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: sidecar.path) before calling persist(survivors); with no sidecar, clear the journal but leave the file intact (the rows stay quarantined and re-journal, which is the correct, non-destructive outcome for an unverified loss). (b) Make the consent honest: rename the control from 'Dismiss' to 'Remove unreadable drops' and put it behind a confirmationDialog naming the count and the irreversibility ('N saved drops can't be read and will be removed from this device. This can't be undone.'), with a plain 'Keep them' escape that only silences the banner for the session. (c) Split the two intents so silencing a banner is never destructive: LocalStoreDiagnostics gains silenceIncident() (journal-only, today's pre-round-12 behaviour) and acceptRowLoss() (the rewrite), and DropsListScreen offers both.

findings.title: After the accepted loss, the reap erases the pending-upload evidence and the ladder climbs to 'Synced — the server has confirmed your drops'
findings.trace: Round 12 made the recorded reap residual reachable. Chain: (1) drop D was created offline — add() (:821-833) persisted it and enqueueCloudSync marked it pending (:949, persisted to defaults at :1109); its sync task ended with .notSignedIn/.ackTimedOut so syncTasks[D] is nil via the defer at :968-970. (2) D's row later becomes undecodable → loadDrops returns .skippedRows (:218), localProvablyClean is false (:650-651) and ProfileScreen shows rung 4 (ProfileScreen.swift:103) — correct and visible. (3) The user taps Dismiss → acknowledgeIncident rewrites the store clean (:269) → acknowledgeReadIncident then kicks refresh(near:) (:720). (4) That refresh loads the rewritten file → .clean (:221). (5) The reap at :601-609 fires on exactly D: syncTasks[D]==nil, D is absent from `drops` (phase 1 at :525 seeds from the published set, which after a relaunch — or after phase 2 replaced it at :591 — no longer holds D), and D carries no tombstone → clearPending(D) (:607). (6) unpushablePendingCount (:483-485) is now 0, localProvablyClean is true (:645-646), incidentMemoryKey was reset to false at :629, so :654-656 latches hasCompletedCleanRefresh and the ProfileScreen ladder falls all the way through to ProfileScreen.swift:152-156, 'Synced — the server has confirmed your drops'. The same convergence happens without any Dismiss whenever a normal save rewrites the store: LocalDropStore.save (:319-327) loads (dropping the bad row) then persists, so the row is gone from disk and the next load is .clean. Structural corollary for the un-pushable rung: ProfileScreen.swift:114-115 requires hasCompletedCleanRefresh && unpushablePendingCount > 0, but the reap at :601 runs earlier in the SAME refresh on precisely the ids that make that count non-zero — so on any .clean load the rung is unreachable by construction. Its only live path is the .absentFile branch, which is exactly what the regression test exercises (DropStoreTests.swift:760-777 uses an absent file and cloudStore: nil). Round 11's B3 restored the latch; this second, independent cause of unreachability was not addressed.
findings.harm: A drop that was never uploaded and has just been destroyed locally leaves zero trace, and the app then asserts positive server confirmation over it. Trigger: user pins a drop while offline in a park; weeks later a bad write damages that row; the banner appears; the user taps Dismiss; on the next launch the Profile tab reads 'Synced — the server has confirmed your drops'. The drop is gone from the device, was never on the server, and no surface — banner, ladder, Sent list — ever says so. This is the fabricated-success failure the wave charter exists to prevent, produced by a single tap.
findings.fix: Make an accepted row loss produce a durable, positive record instead of consuming the evidence. (1) Have LocalStoreDiagnostics.acceptRowLoss (see lens-1c) return the ids it dropped, and give DropLibrary a durable `lostRowIDs` set (defaults key, same persistSet pattern as :1177-1179) seeded from pendingSyncIDs ∩ dropped ids. (2) Add a ladder rung ABOVE 'Synced' in ProfileScreen: 'N drops were removed because they couldn't be read — they were never uploaded' with a Clear control, so the loss survives the reap that erased the pending id. (3) Do not let the reap silently swallow un-pushable evidence: in refresh() (:601-609), before clearPending(id), record the id into lostRowIDs when the reap is the reason it disappeared, and log/emit rather than clear-and-forget. (4) Reachability lock for rung 5: make the un-pushable rung read (pendingSyncIDs ∪ lostRowIDs) so it is reachable on a .clean load, not only on .absentFile.

findings.title: B1's uid gate turned a wrong verdict into an unbounded, unlabelled spinner — the receive flow has no terminal state when the account never connects
findings.trace: ReceiveScreen.swift:55-58: `.task(id: account.uid ?? "-") { guard account.uid != nil, drop == nil else { return }; await load() }`. When uid is nil the task returns immediately and never re-runs, because the id only changes if uid changes. The body (:36-44) then falls to the else branch: a bare ProgressView — no text, no cause, no Try again, no Close (Close exists only inside failedView at :140). The account can stay nil for the whole process lifetime: AccountService.start() (:25-41) is invoked exactly once from AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:30 and (a) returns immediately when AppConfig.firebaseConfigured is false (:26 — AppConfig.swift:13-14, the plist is gitignored, so every build without it), or (b) on a thrown signInAnonymously it sets statusText 'Couldn't reach the account service — retrying on next launch' (:37) and gives up — there is no retry, no listener, no scenePhase re-arm. So in both cases uid is nil forever and the invitation screen spins forever. This is a round-12 regression on the unconfigured path specifically: DropSharingService.fetchSharedDrop already answers that case honestly (:66 → .unknown → ReceiveScreen :124/:131 'This link can't be opened right now… check your connection and try again in a moment' + Try again), but the gate now prevents that call from ever happening. Even with uid present the loading state is unbounded: :156 awaits getDocument(source:.server) with no client timeout and the spinner carries no copy. The same one-shot-sign-in truth is mis-rendered on the ladder: ProfileScreen.swift:78-81 shows 'Connecting…' as rung 1, which is both a progress claim nothing is progressing and a MASK — it outranks the terminal-failure, unresolved-delete and unreadable-drops rungs at :82/:92/:103, so a user whose sign-in failed sees only 'Connecting…' plus the contradicting statusText at :168-170.
findings.harm: The magic link — the product's entire entry point — dead-ends on a silent spinner. Trigger: a recipient installs the app in a basement/on a plane, taps the shared link on first launch; anonymous sign-in throws; the app shows a spinning wheel with no message, no retry and no close, while arHolder.beginRevealWarmup() (:50) keeps the AR session warm and burning battery behind it. Nothing tells them to try again later; on a TestFlight/dev build without GoogleService-Info.plist the same screen spins forever on every open, where round 11 correctly said 'This link can't be opened right now'.
findings.fix: Give the account a three-valued, terminal state and let both surfaces render it. (1) AccountService: replace the implicit nil with `enum Connection { case connecting, ready(String), unavailable(String) }`; set .unavailable on the catch at :36-39 and immediately when !AppConfig.firebaseConfigured at :26; add a bounded retry (3 attempts with backoff, plus a re-arm on scenePhase .active) before latching .unavailable. (2) ReceiveScreen: key the task on that state; on .unavailable (and on a ~8 s watchdog while .connecting) fall through to the existing failure = .unknown branch, which already carries the correct non-causal copy and Try again — the Try again handler should also call account.retry(). (3) Label the loading state ('Opening your link…') and give it a Close control so no state of this screen is an unexplained, inescapable spinner. (4) ProfileScreen: render rung 1 only for .connecting, render .unavailable as an orange problem rung, and move the account rung BELOW the terminal/unresolved-delete/unreadable rungs so a stalled connection can never mask a data problem.

findings.title: 'One-time link' asserts an access-control property the rules and the client do not implement
findings.trace: ReceiveScreen.swift:112 renders 'One-time link · your camera stays private' directly under the Reveal CTA. No mechanism anywhere burns, expires or scopes the link. The deployed ruleset (web/firestore.rules.deployed, drops read rule) grants a GET to ANY signed-in user whose request carries the document id when visibility is in ['link','public']; the v3 draft (web/firestore.rules, allow get) keeps exactly that capability model and its own comment names it ('the dropId UUID is the secret'). The client has no single-use accounting either: DropSharingService.shareURL (:16-18) is a pure function of drop.id, fetchSharedDrop (:65-105) is a plain read with no consumption side effect, and DropLibrary.redeem (:786-817) is explicitly designed to be idempotent across repeat opens ('Redemption is expressed by opening the LINK'). The second half of the sentence is true and mechanically backed (no camera data leaves the device); the first half is not. Six counsel rounds audited the sync copy; this line sits on the one screen a stranger sees and was never checked against its mechanics.
findings.harm: A false expectation about who can see a pinned real-world location. Trigger: a sender pins a drop at their home address for one person and reads 'One-time link'; the recipient forwards the message to a group chat. Every signed-in reader can open it, repeatedly and indefinitely, and see the coordinates, the caption and the recipient's name. The sender was told the link could be used once.
findings.fix: Change the copy to something the mechanics back — e.g. 'Anyone with this link can open it · your camera stays private' (or 'Private link' if a softer register is wanted, since the id is unguessable). If single use is actually desired as product behaviour it is a real feature, not a copy fix: it needs a server-side redemption record (a `redeemedBy` subdocument written on first successful open and checked in the get rule), which belongs in Wave A alongside the v3 deploy; until then the surface must not claim it. Lock the claim to the mechanic in the emulator suite (see test cases).

When any of these lands during the disk write, the early return skips EVERY line of :876-898: `drops.removeAll` (:877), `clearPending` (:891), `clearTerminal` (:892), `markCloudProven` (:889), `markPendingDelete` (:897) and `launchCloudDelete` (:898). remove() still returns success, so remove(contentsOf:) (:903-915) counts no failure and lastPersistError stays nil.
findings.harm: The user deletes a shared drop. The local row is destroyed on disk, but no tombstone is recorded, no cloud delete is ever issued, and no unresolved-delete verdict exists — so ProfileScreen keeps reporting the good state (ProfileScreen.swift:92 rung never fires) while the Firestore document stays live with visibility "link": every recipient's magic link keeps working forever. On the next refresh the row is re-published from the cloud read (DropStore.swift:558-570 → phase 2 at :591) so the deleted drop reappears in the Sent list with no explanation, and if it was still in pendingSyncIDs, reconcileCloud (:928-932) re-UPLOADS the drop the user deleted. Trigger: swipe-delete on Sent (DropsListScreen.swift:119) or the Map context menu (MapScreen.swift:36) while any refresh/add/update lands in the same millisecond window — e.g. the Map's first-location-fix refresh (MapScreen.swift:105-107) or the auth-ready pass on a cold launch (RootView.swift:168).
findings.fix: Guard remove() on a PER-ID mutation generation, never on the publish-path counter. Add `private var mutationGenerations: [UUID: UInt64]`, bump it (for that id only) in add/update/redeem/remove, and re-check `mutationGenerations[drop.id] == generation` after the `local.delete` await; leave `refreshGeneration` for the publish path alone. If the re-check does fire, do not return silently — log and leave the drop in a visible state (the redeem that superseded it already owns the row). Add an assertion-level invariant test that a successful `local.delete` always produces either a tombstone or a receivedViaLink early-return.

findings.title: B1's uid gate has no terminal state: when anonymous sign-in never completes, a link open spins forever with no copy, no retry and no cause
findings.trace: ReceiveScreen.swift:55-58 `.task(id: account.uid ?? "-") { guard account.uid != nil, drop == nil else { return }; await load() }`. `account.uid` is only ever set in AccountService.attach (AccountService.swift:44). It stays nil permanently in two reachable states: (a) AccountService.swift:26 `guard AppConfig.firebaseConfigured else { return }` — the supported local-only build (AppConfig.swift:13-14, README); (b) AccountService.swift:36-39 — `signInAnonymously()` throws (offline/unreachable on a first-ever launch), which sets `statusText` on the Profile tab only and never retries within the session. With uid nil the task body returns immediately, `drop` and `failure` both stay nil, and the body's else-branch at ReceiveScreen.swift:41-43 renders a bare ProgressView. That branch has no Close, no Try again and no text; the sheet is only escapable by swiping it down. Round 11's own blocker text called out this exact first-launch race and the round-12 gate closed the wrong half of it.
findings.harm: The app's primary acquisition path fails silently. A recipient on a brand-new install taps a friend's link on cellular/poor connectivity, anonymous sign-in fails once, and they get an infinite spinner with zero information and no way to retry short of force-quitting and reopening the link. Before round 12 the same state produced a message and a Try-again button. A local-only build (no GoogleService-Info.plist) hits it 100% of the time. This is a fabricated-progress surface — a spinner asserts work in flight when nothing is in flight — squarely against the wave charter.
findings.fix: Give AccountService a published three-state connection phase (`connecting` / `ready(uid)` / `unavailable(reason)`): set `.unavailable` in the `catch` at AccountService.swift:36-39 and immediately when `!AppConfig.firebaseConfigured` at :26. ReceiveScreen keys on it: `.connecting` → spinner with a bounded deadline (e.g. 8 s) that also falls through to `.unknown`; `.unavailable` → the existing `.unknown` failure view with Try again, and make Try again re-invoke `account.start()` before re-fetching. Never leave the loading branch without an exit.

findings.title: A terminal SAVE refusal is treated as proof the server holds the document, re-opening the permanent unretirable delete alarm that masks the whole ladder
findings.trace: DropStore.swift:886-890 marks an id `cloudProven` when `terminalSyncFailureIDs.contains(drop.id)`. A terminal verdict is issued by performCloudSync at :1015-1024 from `DropStoreError.refusedByServer`, produced in FirebaseDropStore.swift:144-155 for gRPC 3/5/7/9/16 AND for any EncodingError — every one of which means the write was REFUSED, i.e. the document was never created. Downstream: remove() issues the delete (:897-898); under the live ruleset a delete of an absent document DENIES — pinned by web/firestore.rules.deployed:34-35 and asserted in web/rules-tests/deployed-rules.test.mjs:56-57 — surfacing as permissionDenied (code 7), which terminalRefusalReason maps as terminal (FirebaseDropStore.swift:246-247), so all three attempts are spent (DropStore.swift:1070,:1084-1087) and :1090 takes the `cloudProvenIDs` branch → `markUnresolvedDelete`. Retirement is then impossible: serverConfirmsAbsent can never answer under v2 (FirebaseDropStore.swift:198-203) and probeAbsenceCapability latches `.denied` so DropStore.swift:678 returns before any probe runs; redeem() (:793-794) can't clear it either because fetchSharedDrop of a non-existent doc yields `.unknown`, not `.found`. Reachable trigger for the terminal verdict without an ack: a revoked/expired anonymous token → UNAUTHENTICATED (16) on every write while `Auth.auth().currentUser?.uid` is still cached (FirebaseDropStore.swift:99), or any future rules/schema mismatch → permissionDenied (the reason the drift lock exists). Round 10 fixed exactly this class with ackedCloudIDs; round 12's third clause undoes it.
findings.harm: A drop that never reached the cloud produces a PERMANENT ProfileScreen rung-3 claim — "1 deletion couldn't finish — the cloud copy may still exist" (ProfileScreen.swift:92-102) — that no code path can retire before the v3 deploy. Because the ladder is an else-if chain, that false alarm then MASKS every lower rung for the rest of the app's life on that device: the local-corruption warning (:103), the un-pushable-outbox problem count (:114), cloud read errors (:129), upload progress (:133) and the honest checking/Synced states. A round-12 change makes an existing failure class less visible, and it fabricates a cloud copy that does not exist.
findings.fix: Delete the `terminalSyncFailureIDs` clause at DropStore.swift:888. Server possession requires a positive artifact: a stamped `ownerUid` (server truth persisted at :989-1001) or a recorded ack (`ackedCloudIDs`). If a refusal class should ever count, split the taxonomy so only refusals on an UPDATE of an existing document (which implies the doc exists) qualify — a refused create never does. Also move `markCloudProven` below the `receivedViaLink` early-return at :896 so the durable set stops accumulating ids for received drops that never get a tombstone.

findings.title: The durable incident memory never records a .readFailed outcome — the one case whose journal write fails with it
findings.trace: DropStore.swift:625-632 records `hadLocalReadIncident` from `localOutcome`, but `localOutcome` is only assigned at :514-516, inside the branch reached after `local.loadDrops` SUCCEEDED. When the read throws, refresh takes the catch at :500-509 and RETURNS at :508, before the switch. So `.readFailed` — which LocalDropStore sets at :200 — can never be the value the switch sees. That is precisely the outcome whose journal is least likely to exist: LocalDropStore.swift:201 writes the incident with `writeIncident`, which is `try?`-swallowed at :301, on the same volume/container whose read just failed. own-B's stated premise was that a failed journal write must not be indistinguishable from no incident; for `.readFailed` it still is. FlakyLocalStore reproduces the outcome (DropStoreTests.swift:1361-1367) but no test asserts the defaults key, so testFailedRefreshEarnsNoPositiveEvidence (:734-755) passes with and without the recorder.
findings.harm: Disk-full or container-unwritable on launch: the store read throws, the journal write throws too, and nothing durable remembers the incident. If the store file is subsequently absent (data-protection lock lifted after the file was already lost, or the failed write truncated it away), the next refresh sees `.absentFile` with `localReadWarning == nil` and `hadLocalReadIncident == false`, so DropStore.swift:646-650 declares local truth provably clean and :654-656 latches `hasCompletedCleanRefresh` — the app presents an emptied library as "Synced — the server has confirmed your drops" (ProfileScreen.swift:152-159) with no banner anywhere.
findings.fix: Record the memory from the failure path too: set `defaults.set(true, forKey: Self.incidentMemoryKey)` inside refresh's catch at DropStore.swift:500-509 (after the generation guard) whenever `await localDiagnostics?.lastLoadOutcome() == .readFailed`, or — cleaner — have LocalDropStore mirror every destructive outcome into the injected defaults at the moment it happens rather than relying on the observer. Keep `.clean` as the only retirement.

findings.title: The corrected uncapped listener prune is unreachable for any drop outside the newest-10 window, because re-invocation is still keyed on the capped set
findings.trace: ReactionService.swift:119-130 prunes against `allSharedKeys`, computed from the FULL `drops` array (the round-12 SURF-lens-4 fix). But listenToMySharedDrops is only called from RootView.swift:155-157, whose task id is `ReactionService.listenKey(for: library.drops, myUid:)`, and listenKey (:97-102) maps over `watchedDrops` which applies `.prefix(10)` (:81-89). Delete an 11th-or-older shared drop (DropsListScreen.swift:119 / MapScreen.swift:36 → DropStore.remove :877): the newest-10 identity list is unchanged, so the key is unchanged, so the task never re-runs and the prune loop never executes for that id — its listener (attached back when the drop was in the top 10) stays registered indefinitely. The same path also means a sign-out (uid → nil) re-runs the task but returns at :112 before pruning anything.
findings.harm: The sender keeps a live Firestore snapshot listener on the reactions subcollection of a drop they deleted — deleting a parent document does not delete its subcollection, and the deployed rules allow any signed-in user to write a reaction (web/firestore.rules.deployed:37-40). A recipient who still has the drop open can react after the take-back and the sender gets a toast (RootView.swift:102-125) naming a drop they removed, with `incomingDropTitle` captured at attach time (ReactionService.swift:132). Secondary: listeners accumulate for the life of the session (billed reads, battery) with no path to release them.
findings.fix: Make the task key describe what is actually subscribed to plus what may need releasing: key on the FULL shared-set identity (the same predicate as `allSharedKeys`), keeping `.prefix(10)` only inside the attach loop at :131. Two lines: extract the shared-set filter into one `nonisolated static func sharedDrops(in:myUid:)` used by listenKey, the prune, and the attach cap. Also move the prune above the `guard let myUid` at :112 so a sign-out releases the previous account's listeners.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified in source. ReceiveScreen.swift:55-58 `.task(id: account.uid ?? "-") { guard account.uid != nil, drop == nil else { return }; await load() }` — when uid is nil the task returns and nothing can ever set `failure`, so body falls to ReceiveScreen.swift:40-44, a bare ProgressView with no copy, no Try again, no Close (Close exists only inside failedView at :140). uid==nil is absorbing: AccountService.swift:25-41 `start()` signs in once; the catch at :36-39 sets statusText and returns; AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:28-35 calls start() exactly once and the scenePhase .active handler (:36-56) refreshes the library (:52) but never re-arms auth. Round 11's ungated task reached DropSharingService.swift:72-74 → `.unknown` → honest retryable screen. ADDITION I VERIFIED that all three reviewers only partly stated: the gate is not needed for correctness. Under the live v2 rules an unauthenticated read is denied → throws → DropSharingService.swift:72-74 → `.unknown`, and `.task(id:)` re-fires when the uid arrives, so the ungated path self-heals and never fabricates a verdict. The gate bought a cosmetic flash and paid with the only terminal state the screen had.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Two-stage. (1) MINIMUM (5 lines, no new types, ships this round): make the wait BOUNDED instead of absorbing — `.task(id: account.uid ?? "-") { guard drop == nil else { return }; if account.uid == nil { try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(8)); guard !Task.isCancelled, drop == nil else { return } }; await load() }`. Sign-in arriving cancels and re-runs the task with the new id (immediate load); sign-in never arriving falls through to the existing honest `.unknown` + Try again. This is the standard bounded-wait-then-degrade pattern; an unbounded wait on an external dependency is the defect. (2) STRUCTURAL (schedule with Wave A): give AccountService a published `enum Connection { case connecting, ready(String), unavailable(String) }` set `.unavailable` in the catch at AccountService.swift:36-39 and when `!AppConfig.firebaseConfigured` at :26, plus `retry()` (3 attempts, exponential backoff, re-armed on scenePhase .active — the Firebase Auth SDK does not retry a failed signInAnonymously for you). ReceiveScreen's Try again calls retry() before load(); label the loading state and give it a Close. Also reorder ProfileScreen.swift:78-81 — the `account.uid == nil` "Connecting…" rung is FIRST in the else-if chain, so a permanently failed sign-in masks the terminal-sync (:82), unresolved-delete (:92) and unreadable-drops (:103) rungs for the whole session; render `.connecting` as rung 1 but `.unavailable` as a problem rung BELOW the three data rungs.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified in source and it is the inverse of the pattern the same file blesses. DropStore.swift:796-805: `if !drops.contains(where: id) { drops.insert(drop, at: 0); do { try await local.save(drop) } catch { lastPersistError = …; throw error } }` — in-memory insert BEFORE the disk write, and the catch does not roll the insert back. add() at :821-833 deliberately persists first and inserts only after success (its own comment: "The in-memory insert happens only AFTER the disk write succeeds"). The round-12 B4 predicate then keys the whole write decision on `drops.contains`, so after a failed first redeem the retry takes the empty branch, `hadTombstone` is false so :813 does nothing, and the function returns normally — no throw, no banner, nothing persisted. The vacuity claim also holds: both round-12 redeem tests miss it (DropStoreTests.swift:855-884 puts the row on disk via add() first; :996-1020 exercises only the no-row branch).
verdicts.industrialSolution: Mirror add(): write-ahead, then publish. Move `drops.insert(drop, at: 0)` below a successful `try await local.save(drop)` so in-memory presence really does imply on-disk presence (option (b), rolling back in the catch, is equivalent but leaves a window where a concurrent reader sees a row that is about to vanish). This is the same durability ordering rule the whole store already follows — the authoritative predicate must be checked against the authority (disk), not against a cache of it. Pair with the state-3 fix (hoist the own-drop recall above the throw) since both live in the same 20 lines, and add the missing FlakyLocalStore `setFailSave(ids:)` knob so the branch is testable at all.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified. DropStore.swift:748 `let changed = evidenceUid != nil && evidenceUid != uid`; `evidenceUid` is per-instance in-memory state (:429) on a DropLibrary constructed fresh per process (AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:18), so on the only auth-ready call of a launch it is nil and `changed` is false — the revalidation loop at :755-762 never runs. Grep confirms `accountDidChange()` (:728-737), which round 11 ran on every auth-ready firing and which unconditionally re-enqueued every terminal id, now has ZERO production callers (only DropStoreTests.swift:846). No other path re-attempts a terminal id: performCloudSync clears it from pendingSyncIDs when it goes terminal (:1012-1013, :1021-1023) and reconcileCloud only iterates pendingSyncIDs/pendingDeleteIDs (:928-936). The only recovery left is manual and per-drop (ShareDropSheet.swift:201-209). Reachable trigger is real: FirebaseDropStore.swift:246-250 maps permissionDenied(7) and unauthenticated(16) to a terminal verdict, and both are transient-in-practice conditions (token refresh failure, a rules deploy window) that this app cannot re-attempt automatically any more.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Distinguish the two things round 12 merged: the LATCH resets on an identity change; the terminal-verdict RETRY resets on a new session. Both are correct triggers for their own concern. `let firstPassThisSession = (evidenceUid == nil)` before :749, then `if changed || firstPassThisSession { for id in terminalSyncFailureIDs { … } }`. This preserves cross-cutting rule 4 — the verdict is still revoked only by the server ack in performCloudSync (:974-976), never by the retry itself — and restores the automatic recovery round 11 had. Industrially this is standard non-retryable-error handling: a 'permanent' failure is re-attempted exactly once per new authentication context, never in a loop. Bound it (cap the revalidation at N ids per pass, reusing the probe cap pattern at :682) so a large terminal set cannot storm the outbox on launch. Then delete `accountDidChange()` and DropStoreTests.swift:842-851 — a test of a method production cannot call is worse than no test.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced empirically, and the practical exposure is HIGHER than the reviewer stated. drift-check.mjs:41 extracts with `/^\s*var (\w+)\s*[:=]/gm`. Against a fixture of the real struct plus `let sessionTag: String` and `@ServerTimestamp var commitAt: Date?` the extractor returned exactly ['id','emoji','uid','byName','at'] — both new fields silently dropped; the widened pattern `/^\s*(?:@\w+(?:\([^)]*\))?\s+)*(?:var|let)\s+(\w+)\s*[:=]/gm` returned all seven. Swift's synthesized Codable encodes `let` stored properties and attributed stored properties identically to `var`, so both would ship a key that firestore.rules:78's hasOnly list forbids. THE ELEVATION: the next scheduled change on the counsel's own list — the seams-5/flows-4 serverTimestamp toast watermark — is precisely `@ServerTimestamp var commitAt: Date?`, the attributed form the regex misses. And the emulator suite cannot back it up: rules.test.mjs:95-97 builds the reaction payload as a HARD-CODED literal `{ id, emoji, uid, byName, at }` (it derives the emoji list from appEmojiList() at :98 but not the key list), so it proves nothing about the shipping struct. The rulesReactionKeys anchor concern (:46 matches the first hasOnly in the file) is currently benign — firestore.rules has exactly one — but the scheduled seams-3 field-mask would insert one ahead of it.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Do not parse declaration syntax to predict encoder output — assert the encoder's output. (1) Add `testDropReactionEncodesExactlyTheRuleAllowedKeys` in the device bundle: `JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: JSONEncoder().encode(DropReaction(emoji:"❤️",uid:"u",byName:"n")))` → assert the key Set equals a pinned literal. That fails for ANY encoded-shape change regardless of `var`/`let`/property wrappers/CodingKeys. (2) Make the emulator suite derive its payload from the same source: build the reaction object in rules.test.mjs from `appReactionKeys()` so a new key makes the 'every UI emoji writable' assertions fail against the real ruleset. (3) Keep the regex but make it fail CLOSED — widen it as above AND throw on any line in the struct body it cannot classify. (4) Anchor rulesReactionKeys to the `match /drops/{dropId}/reactions` block rather than the first hasOnly. Item (1)+(2) must land BEFORE the commitAt field and before the v3 deploy, or the first reaction after deploy is PERMISSION_DENIED → refusedByServer → terminal verdict on every reaction.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified: DropStore.swift:886-890 runs the markCloudProven capture BEFORE the received-drop early return at :896 (`guard cloud != nil, drop.receivedViaLink != true else { return }`). verdicts.verdictNote: recreation concern refuted; deployed-LIST gap confirmed
verdicts.reasoning: REFUTED on its stated mechanism. Firestore security rules are stateless with respect to document history: at evaluation time `resource` is either the current document or null. A create following a delete is indistinguishable from any other create — there is no rules-expressible predicate 'this id was previously deleted', so the hypothesised hardening ('gating create on resource == null plus an id-reuse check') cannot be written, and no rules assertion can pin it. B2's correctness rests on two SDK guarantees, not rules: (a) Firestore's local mutation queue is applied in order per document, and (b) `setData(..., merge: true)` — FirestoreAcked.swift:31-34 defaults merge true, used by FirebaseDropStore.swift:129-132 — is a precondition-free patch that CREATES the document if absent. Both are documented, universal SDK behaviours; an emulator rules test would assert neither. CONFIRMED on the incidental half: deployed-rules.test.mjs (5 assertions, :49-64) does not pin the owner-scoped LIST query the client issues on every refresh (FirebaseDropStore.swift:64-66 `whereField("ownerUid", isEqualTo: uid).getDocuments()`); that shape is pinned only against v3 (rules.test.mjs:73-74). Under v2's combined `allow read` a filtered list is permitted, but nothing in the repo asserts it, so a v2 hotfix could break every refresh with a green suite.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Do not add the recreation assertion — it would be a test that cannot fail for the reason it claims, which is a review defect of its own. Instead: (1) add the owner-scoped LIST assertion to deployed-rules.test.mjs so both suites pin the same client dependencies; (2) if the counsel wants B2's real dependency locked, the correct instrument is an integration test against the Firestore emulator with a real client SDK — `disableNetwork()` → deleteDoc → setDoc(merge:true) → `enableNetwork()` → assert getDoc(source:.server).exists — which exercises queue ordering and merge-upsert, the two facts B2 actually depends on. That belongs in the Wave A emulator harness, not the rules suite.

verdicts.findingId: state-1 (= flows:lens-1 — one root, two reviewers converged)
verdicts.reasoning: The most consequential defect in the build, and BOTH halves are round-12 code. Verified: remove() bumps the GLOBAL publish counter at DropStore.swift:858 (`refreshGeneration &+= 1`), captures it at :859, awaits `local.delete(drop)` at :863 — a real suspension (DropLibrary is @MainActor at :355; LocalDropStore is an actor at :137 and delete does a full load+persist at :329-333) — then at :872-875 returns before ALL bookkeeping if the counter moved. refresh() bumps the same counter synchronously at :491 before its first await, and is fired from AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:34 and :52 (the round-12 scenePhase-.active refresh), DropsListScreen.swift:26 (the toolbar button on the SAME screen as the swipe-delete at :113-121), MapScreen.swift:105-107 (Explore tab, same screen as the context-menu delete at :36), RootView.swift:168 and DropStore.swift:720; add/update/redeem bump it too, and GeoARSessionManager calls update on every persisted placement edit. When the abort fires, the disk row is ALREADY destroyed (:863) and none of :877-898 runs: no drops.removeAll, no in-flight-upload cancel, no provenance capture, no clearPending/clearTerminal, and critically no markPendingDelete/launchCloudDelete. remove() returns normally, so remove(contentsOf:) at :903-915 counts zero failures and no banner appears. Harm confirmed by tracing the publish: phase 1 is now additive (:525-529) and re-seeds the stale row from `drops`, so with a failing/absent cloud read the row lingers in memory this session and is simply gone at relaunch — while the Firestore document and every recipient's magic link stay live forever with no tombstone and no unresolved-delete rung. Coverage confirmed nil: testDeleteDuringRefreshIsNotResurrectedByThePublish (DropStoreTests.swift:369-389) parks the refresh BEFORE remove bumps, so remove's guard passes and the new branch is never entered.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Per-entity optimistic concurrency, not a global publish counter — the standard fix for 'did MY row change under me'. Add `private var rowGenerations: [UUID: UInt64]` bumped ONLY by add/update/redeem for that specific id; remove() captures `rowGenerations[drop.id]` before `await local.delete` and re-checks only that afterwards, leaving refreshGeneration to the publish path it was built for. This preserves the STATE-lens-6 intent exactly (a redeem landing mid-delete still owns the row) and makes a read-only refresh incapable of voiding a destructive intent. Second, the abort must not be a bare `return`: the disk row is gone either way, so on a detected supersession either (a) re-verify the row is back on disk and complete the tombstone bookkeeping if it is not, or (b) at minimum set a visible verdict — an unannounced early return from a half-completed destructive transition is the failure the charter forbids. Third, add the missing test capability: FlakyLocalStore (DropStoreTests.swift:1346-1390) has no delete gate; give it setGateDelete/parkedDeleteCount/releaseAllDeletes mirroring GatedCloudStore (cross-cutting rule 6) and assert pendingDeleteIDs.contains(id) && cloud.deleteAttempts >= 1 after a refresh lands during the parked delete.

verdicts.reasoning: Mechanically correct and a clean cross-cutting-rule-4 violation, with the reviewer's own honest reachability caveat upheld. `hasCompletedCleanRefresh` is set at DropStore.swift:654-656 and cleared in exactly two places — accountDidChange (:731, now callerless) and authDidBecomeReady on a real uid change (:751). `localProvablyClean` (:642-653) returning false for .skippedRows/.quarantinedWholeFile/.readFailed only fails to SET the latch; it never revokes a standing one. In-session chain verified: refresh #1 clean → latch true; file becomes unreadable → refresh #2 quarantines → latch survives, but localReadWarning covers it at ProfileScreen.swift:103-113; user taps Dismiss → acknowledgeReadIncident (:706-722) clears the warning and for a whole-file quarantine does NOT rewrite anything → ladder falls through :145 to 'Synced — the server has confirmed your drops' (:152-156) over an emptied library. Reachability is genuinely thin (the app writes atomically, so in-session corruption is externally caused), which is why I rate it below the other confirmed items — but the fix is one line and the rule is binding.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Revoke on positive evidence of loss, symmetrically with the durable-memory write that already exists in the same switch: at DropStore.swift:625-632 add `hasCompletedCleanRefresh = false` to the `case .skippedRows?, .quarantinedWholeFile?, .readFailed?` arm, and set it false on the throwing-load abort path at :500-509 too. General principle: any latched positive verdict needs an explicit revocation edge for every condition that falsifies its precondition; a latch with a set-edge and no clear-edge is a bug waiting for a trigger.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified: redeem() clears both tombstone sets at DropStore.swift:793-795 BEFORE the persist block, and the persist catch at :800-803 rethrows — control never reaches the B2 re-upload enqueue at :813-816. The tombstone is already gone, so nothing will re-issue or compensate for the delete still sitting in Firestore's durable mutation queue, and RootView.swift:64-72 shows the user only 'Couldn't save this drop — it may disappear after this session', which describes the local row. Compound and rare (needs a staged delete AND a failing disk write), but the failure is invisible in the one dimension that matters — the shared link — and the fix is mechanical. Correctly identified as passing under the existing test (DropStoreTests.swift:975-991 uses a healthy local store).
verdicts.industrialSolution: Order the irreversible remote compensation ahead of the recoverable local one. Capture `let shouldRecall = hadTombstone && drop.receivedViaLink != true` up front, and enqueue the re-upload (from the fetched copy when no local row survives) BEFORE rethrowing the persist error — or wrap it in a `defer`. Recalling a queued cloud delete has no dependency on the local disk write succeeding; coupling them makes the disk the single point of failure for a remote-state repair. Combine with the seams-2 reordering in one edit.

verdicts.verdictNote: defect confirmed; the stated harm chain is PARTIAL
verdicts.reasoning: CONFIRMED on the defect. DropStore.swift:263-278 acknowledgeIncident(): for `.skippedRows` it re-reads, decodes, and `persist(survivors)` — the unreadable rows are overwritten out of drops.json. The only UI control is DropsListScreen.swift:58-68, a button literally titled 'Dismiss' with no consent copy, no count, no alert. The code's own justification at :260-261 ('their original bytes are already preserved in the digest sidecar') is an UNCHECKED precondition: preserveUnreadable (:285-298) returns false on a failed sidecar write and the caller only downgrades the user-facing string (:213-215); lastOutcome stays `.skippedRows` (:218) so the `if case .skippedRows?` at :264 matches and rewrites anyway. I independently verified the sidecar is a dead end even on the success path: no code anywhere reads `unreadable-*` (grep: preserveUnreadable is the only producer, and the only other references are test assertions), and Config/Info.plist declares NEITHER UIFileSharingEnabled NOR LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace, so the user can never reach those bytes. Pre-round-12 acknowledgement only removed the journal note, so the rows survived. PARTIAL on the harm chain: the reviewer's headline trigger (device low on free space) largely self-protects — `persist` writes with .atomic (:337-340), so on a genuinely full volume the rewrite throws and :271-274 returns early keeping the journal and the rows. The residual real harm is (a) any non-space sidecar failure (occupied path, protection class) where the smaller survivors file still fits, and (b) the always-true case: even with a successful sidecar, recoverable JSON is destroyed from the only location any future app version would look, behind a button labelled 'Dismiss'.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Do not solve a re-journaling problem with a destructive write. The round-11 item (SURF-lens-5) was 'the incident is un-dismissable because the kicked refresh re-journals it'; the industrial answer is IDEMPOTENT INCIDENT IDENTITY, not data deletion: record the acknowledged incident's content digest (preserveUnreadable already computes SHA256 at :286-288) in the journal/defaults, and have loadDrops suppress re-journaling when the digest matches an acknowledged one. Dismiss then means dismiss, the rows stay recoverable, and the banner does not come back. If the counsel still wants an explicit accept-the-loss action, split the two intents: `silenceIncident()` (journal-only, digest-keyed) and `acceptRowLoss()` (the rewrite), the latter gated on a verified sidecar (`FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: sidecar.path)`, recorded alongside lastOutcome) AND behind a confirmationDialog naming the count and irreversibility, with the control renamed 'Remove unreadable drops'. Destructive-action UX rule: the label must name the destruction, the confirmation must name the count, and the precondition the code cites must be asserted, not assumed.

verdicts.reasoning: CONFIRMED, including the corollary I initially doubted and then verified against source. verdicts.reasoning: The highest-value finding in the round and the clearest regression against a fix the counsel already made. Verified end to end. Treating a refused CREATE as proof of server possession is exactly inverted. Retirement is then IMPOSSIBLE: I grepped every clearUnresolvedDelete caller — :689 (server-confirmed absence, which v2 can never answer; probeAbsenceCapability latches .denied and :678 returns before any probe) and :794 (redeem, unreachable because fetchSharedDrop of a non-existent doc yields .unknown, not .found). Round 10's ackedCloudIDs work fixed exactly this class; round 12's third clause reopens it.

Server possession requires a positive artifact of possession: a stamped ownerUid (server truth persisted at :989-1001) or a recorded ack (ackedCloudIDs) — both already in the predicate, and both already cover the one refusal that DOES imply existence (ownedByAnotherAccount can only be produced by FirebaseDropStore.swift:109-111 when drop.ownerUid is already non-nil, so the first clause subsumes it). If a refusal class should ever count as evidence, it must be split by operation: a refused UPDATE of an existing document implies existence; a refused CREATE proves the opposite. This is binding rule 1 applied to an alarm rather than a good state — the claim 'the cloud copy may still exist' is itself a positive assertion and needs positive evidence. verdicts.reasoning: Verified: the round-12 prune fix is real but unreachable for the drops it was built for.
